data.title: R12 manual proof and the plan's acceptance line are not in the evidence; no real-manager install has been observed
data.detail:
The plan's acceptance_line (accepted at gate 3, seq 25) requires, beyond build/test/lint: "a SUPERVISED session started from the built CLI on a scratch repo with pnpm-lock.yaml prints a record whose install.exitCode is 0 and whose worktree runs node -e \"require('better-sqlite3')\" with exit 0; the same start with an outdated lockfile exits 1 printing ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE on stderr and leaves no session record." Spec R12 and plan Proof items 1–3 say those outputs are "pasted verbatim into the round".

What the change carries instead:
- log.jsonl seq 39 (session sess-xmx6sz41t2) and seq 40 (harness session c22017d0-…) are the only rounds; each has exactly three results: build, test, lint. No `note` event from the build session, no other round.
- .sdlc-state/sessions/sess-xmx6sz41t2/rounds.jsonl: one round, the same three results.
- pr.yaml on main: checks = evidence (per-change run 2 green · 3/3 verification commands) and evals (no eval cases intersect the diff). evals/run-2.json commandResults: build, test, lint.
- Commit messages 3f3be2e^1..f300b75 carry no output.

So the only path that runs `sh -c` with a manager is install.test.ts, where `pnpm` is a fake shell script in a temp bin/. The real `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` through the launcher has never been observed: this review session (sess-9gm7crk0c2, session.started at 2026-09-11T07:44:32Z, seq 33 on main) was launched 15 s before the gate-5 merge (3f3be2e, 07:44:47Z), its session.started has no `install` field and its state dir (.sdlc-state/sessions/sess-9gm7crk0c2/) has context.json, mcp.json, prompt.md, stream.jsonl and no install.log — the pre-merge console, as C9 predicted. The intent's done signal (a green first verify-before-done round) therefore remains unobserved.

One part of C4 is settled by inspection, not by the change: better-sqlite3@13.0.3 in this worktree's store ships prebuilds/ (darwin-arm64.node, darwin-x64.node, linux-*.node, win32-*.node) and has no build/ directory, so pnpm 10's build-script policy does not matter for it. The frozen offline install through the launcher on a real repository (R12 item 2) and the ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE refusal through the CLI (item 3) are still unproven; the first post-merge launch with the console restarted is the earliest proof.

data.title: Engine-launched sessions keep only the one-line message of a failed install; the output exists nowhere
data.detail:
Spec R6: "an engine job that launched the session fails with the same message and the output in its `error`, so the Jobs list on the Sessions view shows it." The PR does not touch engine.ts, and every engine path stores only the message:
- engine.ts:689 (`launch`, used for auto build/review/propose sessions): `this.opts.jobs.update(key, { state: "failed", error: (e as Error).message }, …)`; line 690 logs the same message.
- engine.ts:869 (auto-resume after the first red run): `error: (e as Error).message`.
- engine.ts:257 (band diagnose/propose sessions): `error: (e as Error).message`.
`installFailure` (install.ts:370-372) puts the whole output only in `diagnostics[0].message`; `ActionError.message` is "dependency install failed in <checkout>: <command> exited <code>". Because the throw happens before `deps.registry.upsert` and before `mkdirSync(stateDir)` (launcher.ts:168-178), there is no session record, no card and no install.log for a refused launch. On the engine path (sdlc serve --engine, the production mode for AUTO builds, stage-5 reviews at engine.ts:591-593, band sessions, and auto-resume) the manager's output is therefore dropped entirely; the person sees "exited 1" in the Jobs list and has to re-run the install by hand to learn why (e.g. ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE vs. a missing pnpm on PATH vs. a timeout).

Plan step 4 took this narrower reading explicitly ("The output itself travels in diagnostics (HTTP body, CLI stderr) … That is the R6 reading this plan takes") and the plan was accepted, so this is a known deviation from the spec; it is reported because it contradicts the accepted R6 text and the non-negotiable that evidence is shown verbatim on exactly the path where nobody is watching a terminal. The smallest fix is one line per site, e.g. `error: e instanceof ActionError && e.diagnostics.length ? `${e.message}\n${e.diagnostics.map(d => d.message).join("\n")}` : e.message` — the plan already checked that the job store keeps `error` unshortened.

data.title: planMatches: false comes from the accepted plan on main lacking change-export.schema.json; the branch amended plan.md in place without a revision
data.detail:
pr.yaml on main records `planMatches: false`. evals/run-2.json fileSet (16 files) includes `packages/schemas/json/change-export.schema.json`; the plan accepted at gate 3 (log.jsonl seq 25, artifactSha d474f3264e401ba705d1512f61356a4301ded348, rev 2) lists 15 files and not that one. The runner computes the check from main's view (runner.ts:154, `check.planSync(fileSet, view.planFiles, …)`, checks.ts:24-35), so the one unplanned file makes the PR "no".

On the branch, commit 936ce7d ("sdlc(schemas): session.started carries the dependency install") edited plan.md in the same commit — adding the file to "Files that change" and one sentence to step 3 — which checks.ts:25-26 accepts ("plan.md changes in the same commit — plan revision recorded"; hook.allowed plan-sync at seq 31–38). The front matter was left as rev 2 with `accepted_by`/`accepted_at` intact and no `plan.drafted`/`plan.final` event was appended, so the merged plan.md (blob 0e14421 on main) no longer matches the sha gate 3 accepted, while the ledger says rev 2 is what was accepted. The addition itself is correct (the generator rewrites both JSON files and the drift test checks both). This is for the code owner's awareness: either the "plan.md in the same commit" path should bump `rev` and record an event, or the PR's planMatches should be read from the branch's own plan-sync verdicts (derive.ts:298-302 already does this for the change view when the events are present) — a system question outside this change, not a defect in the diff.

data.title: The install runs a fetched PR branch's package lifecycle scripts unconditionally at review launch
data.detail:
INSTALL_COMMANDS (install.ts:281-285) pass no `--ignore-scripts`: `npm ci` runs every dependency's install scripts and `pnpm install` runs the root package's own preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare (pnpm 10 only skips *dependencies'* build scripts; the repo declares no `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies`). prepareWorktree runs on every launch, including `kind === "review"` on a checkout that engine.fetchBranch (engine.ts:432-445) created from origin, and the engine auto-launches one review session per PR head at stage 5 (engine.ts:591-593). In hosted mode with webhooks a pull request from an external fork therefore has its package.json scripts and lockfile-selected packages executed as the console's user, at launch, before any person has read the diff, with no record if the install fails (see the R6 finding).

Severity is low because the trust boundary was already crossed: the harness is launched in the same worktree with the branch's `.claude/**` hooks and CLAUDE.md, so branch-controlled code ran at session start before this change. The install adds a second, unconditional path that the spec (R1, C6 "every launch") requires without weighing untrusted branches. If the owner wants a line of defence, the cheapest is `--ignore-scripts` for review-kind launches only (a new session kind branch in prepareWorktree, no config or opt-out key, so C8 holds); otherwise a sentence in decisions.md that review worktrees are trusted like the harness is enough.
